rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Concept 5: Connection between Linear Expansion and other topics  ·  Key Formula 5: Important relation in Linear Expansion  ·  ❌ All solids expand at the same rate. ✅ Different materials have very different $\alpha$ values. Invar ($\alpha \approx 1.2 \times 10^{-6}$) expands 24 times less than aluminum ($\alpha \approx 24 \times 10^{-6}$).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The coefficient $\alpha$ has units of temperature. ✅ $\alpha$ has units of K⁻¹ (or °C⁻¹). It is a fractional change per degree, not an absolute change.  ·  ❌ A hole in a metal plate shrinks when heated. ✅ The hole EXPANDS — the material around it expands outward, making the hole larger. This is equivalent to a disk of the same material expanding.  ·  ❌ Linear expansion applies to liquids. ✅ Liquids do not have a fixed shape, so linear expansion is meaningless for them. Only cubical (volume) expansion is defined for liquids.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The expansion gap for railway tracks should be as large as possible. ✅ The gap must be just large enough to prevent buckling. Too large a gap causes excessive noise and wear at the joints.  ·  ❌ Thermal stress depends only on $\alpha$ and $\Delta T$. ✅ Thermal stress is $\sigma = Y\alpha\Delta T$ — it also depends on Young's modulus $Y$. A stiffer material develops more stress for the same constraint.  ·  Note 3: Practice numerical problems regularly for mastery of Linear Expansion
